text:
maria: FYI noticed a user report where our Go SDK returns a generic 500 for what looks like rate limiting. stack trace below, they hit this while spinning up many short requests

maria: ```
2024-05-10T15:02:12Z ERROR client.go:182 request failed status=500 body="{\"error\":\"server_error\"}"
github.com/redwood/sdk-go.(*Client).Do
	...
```

akash: hmm. Do we upstream-return 429 for rate limits? I thought our API returns 429 + Retry-After for quota hits.

maria: yes on the hosted API it is 429. But this user is behind a gateway that sometimes transforms errors (we saw a proxy injecting a 500 for a short window). The problem is the Go SDK surfaces it as an opaque 500 error type, so callers can't do typed backoff.

ben: Got it. So two problems: (1) mapping of status code->SDK exception type, (2) preserving Retry-After metadata when available.

julia: Are other SDKs (py/js) converting non-200 codes into distinct typed exceptions? I vaguely recall Python exposes RateLimitError with retry_after attr.

akash: Python returns redwood.errors.RateLimitError for 429 and attaches retry_after (float seconds). JS does similar. Go currently only returns an *APIError with Status int and Body string. No typed helpers.

maria: Exactly. This causes parity issues for customers migrating between SDKs or following sample app recipes that suggest "if RateLimitError -> sleep then retry".

ben: Minimal approach: add a sentinel typed error in Go: var ErrRateLimit = errors.New("rate limit") and wrap APIError with errors.Is/As support and include RetryAfter header field on the struct. That keeps API surface small but programmatic.

maria: Sketch of usage for user:

maria: ```go
resp, err := client.CreateCompletion(ctx, req)
if errors.Is(err, redwood.ErrRateLimit) {
    // get retry info if available
    if aerr, ok := err.(redwood.APIError); ok && aerr.RetryAfter > 0 {
        time.Sleep(time.Duration(aerr.RetryAfter) * time.Second)
    }
    // retry...
}
```

julia: That looks reasonable. We should also ensure the doc quickstart sample uses the pattern. I can patch the Go sample app.

akash: One gotcha: some users behind the proxy won't get Retry-After, so we should recommend exponential backoff default. Also log when mapping 500->RateLimit so we can monitor false-positives.

deploy-bot: deploy: go-sdk/patch/429-errtype -> staging succeeded (build #2345) :rocket:

ben: Nice. Maria can you open a tiny RFC in devex/rdx describing the change and plan to ship in the next patch release? We'll need a short changelog entry and a breaking-note? I think it's additive so not breaking.

maria: Will do. I'll open PR with errtype + RetryAfter parsing + update sample app and a one-paragraph doc change. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/2345 (draft).

akash: Suggest adding a small unit test that fakes a 429 with Retry-After and an integration test covering a 500 that contains the rate-limit body so we can be confident mapping is correct.

maria: yup adding tests. Also will add telemetry event "sdk.rate_limit_mapped" so we can track frequency and source (proxy vs origin)

ben: thumbs-up. Thanks for catching this early — good DX win, especially for sample apps and onboarding guides.

maria: thanks — assigning to @ben to review when PR ready, pinging @julia to update Go quickstart afterwards.

julia: will update quickstart and the snippet under "retries".

maria: closing the loop here once PR merged.
